items.stem: Describe three modes of occurrence of minerals.
items.answer: (1) In igneous and metamorphic rocks in cracks, faults or joints as veins and lodes. (2) In sedimentary rocks in beds or layers. (3) By decomposition of surface rocks, e.g. bauxite. (4) As placer deposits in river sands, and in ocean waters and beds.

items.stem:

(b) Why do we need to conserve minerals? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Most metallic minerals, coal and mica occur in the old crystalline rocks of the peninsular plateau. (2) Most petroleum deposits are in the sedimentary rocks of Gujarat and Assam. (3) Rajasthan, with the rock systems of the peninsula, has many non-ferrous minerals. (4) The alluvial plains of north India are almost devoid of economic minerals. (b) (1) Minerals are finite and non-renewable. (2) Their formation takes millions of years while we use them fast.

items.stem: Explain the uses and distribution of bauxite and mica in India.
items.answer: (1) Bauxite gives aluminium, which is light, strong and a good conductor. (2) Bauxite deposits are in the Amarkantak plateau, Maikal hills and Koraput district of Odisha.
